E1.evidence: Issue #679 is a planned API refactoring, not a defect report: "On the [last WG meeting](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1818AoYucI2z82awL_-8sAA5pMCV_g_wXCJiM6SQmhSQ/edit#heading=h.6726bri1lla5) it was decided to force use of `get_node()` getter in controllers. For this `node_` member should be made private." It is tagged as a good-first-issue task and reports no failure, reproducer, or error log. The fix PRs implement the refactor in two coordinated steps (ros2_control#699 "Updated node_ to private and added the function everywhere node_ was used previously."; ros2_controllers#329 "Replaced node_ everywhere with get_node() and with get_node_const() inside const functions.", which "Depends on: ros2_control/pull/699"). Additional context: During review of ros2_control#699 the PR author reports a build break between the in-progress provider (node_ private, get_node() non-const) and the in-progress consumer changes of ros2_controllers#329: "`joint_trajectory_controller.cpp` wasn't building because some of it's const methods couldn't guarantee the node wouldn't be modified without a const getter function." with the compiler error "error: passing ‘const joint_trajectory_controller::JointTrajectoryController’ as ‘this’ argument discards qualifiers [-fpermissive]" (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/pull/699, review comment on controller_interface.hpp). This was resolved inside the same PR by adding a const overload of get_node() (merged header declares both get_node() and get_node() const). Both sides were unreleased PR heads written together, so this is development churn of the refactor rather than a defect of a composition; it is recorded here only for completeness. ros2_control#699 merged 2022-04-24 (8b29c2770f2e0ec59b8a9673de33c12756a9613f); ros2_controllers#329 merged 2022-04-25 (53d3b25564ac82211af8c24ef47d47169015f6dd). Also discussed in #699: a CI test failure "free(): invalid pointer" in controller_manager tests, which a reviewer judged unrelated ("The test that is failing is having other issues. It is not related to this PR.").

E2.evidence: Not evaluated beyond E1. The two units that the refactor touches are the controller_interface library (ros2_control) and the controllers in ros2_controllers that accessed the protected node_ member; the interface is the ControllerInterface C++ API (node_, get_node()).

E3.evidence: Not evaluated beyond E1. Had a failure been documented it would have been an UPGRADE (controllers written against a controller_interface that exposed node_).
